categories.main_business_segments: CenterPoint Energy operates through three main business segments: Electric, Natural Gas, and Corporate and Other. The Electric segment includes electric transmission, distribution, and generation services in Texas (Houston Electric) and Indiana (SIGECO/Indiana Electric). The Natural Gas segment provides regulated natural gas sales, transportation, and storage services across Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, Ohio, and Texas. The Corporate and Other segment includes corporate support functions and, until mid-2023, energy performance contracting services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include electric transmission and distribution infrastructure, advanced metering systems (AMS), and regulated natural gas distribution networks. Electric generation in Indiana utilizes coal, natural gas, landfill gas, and solar, with a transition toward renewables and battery storage. The company employs grid modernization, resiliency investments, and advanced automation for reliability, and uses structured commodity price stabilization and storage for natural gas supply management.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers are residential, commercial, industrial, and transportation users of electricity and natural gas. In Texas, Houston Electric serves retail electric providers (REPs) who supply end customers, while Indiana Electric serves direct retail customers. The Natural Gas segment serves a broad base of residential and commercial customers across six states, with major metropolitan areas including Houston, Minneapolis, Shreveport, Biloxi, Evansville, and Dayton.
categories.geographic_coverage: CenterPoint Energy’s operations are concentrated in the U.S., primarily in Texas (Houston/Galveston area), Indiana (southwestern region), Minnesota, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Ohio. The company’s electric operations are focused in Texas and Indiana, while its natural gas operations span six states, with a pending divestiture of Louisiana and Mississippi gas businesses.
categories.supply_chain_position: CenterPoint Energy operates as a regulated utility at the downstream end of the energy supply chain, delivering electricity and natural gas to end users. In Indiana, it is vertically integrated for electric generation, transmission, and distribution, while in Texas, it focuses on transmission and distribution. The company also manages pipeline interconnections and storage for natural gas distribution.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include grid modernization, system resiliency, and a transition to cleaner energy sources, with a ten-year capital plan of nearly $47.5 billion through 2030. The company is executing a generation transition plan in Indiana to retire coal assets and add renewables, and has set net zero goals for Scope 1 and certain Scope 2 emissions by 2035, with a 20-30% reduction target for certain Scope 3 emissions. Innovation efforts include deployment of advanced metering, automation, and pilot projects in renewable natural gas and hydrogen.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through regulated rates for electric transmission, distribution, and generation services, as well as natural gas sales, transportation, and storage. Rates are set by state and local regulators, with cost recovery mechanisms for capital investments, fuel, and purchased power. The company also receives revenue from long-term power purchase agreements and, until recently, from energy performance contracting.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: CenterPoint Energy is a leading regulated utility in its service territories, facing limited direct competition due to exclusive service areas for transmission and distribution. In Texas, it is the sole TDU in its region, while in Indiana it is a vertically integrated utility. Competition in natural gas comes from alternative energy sources and, in some areas, from other pipelines and marketers. Major REP customers include affiliates of NRG and Vistra Energy Corp.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2024, CenterPoint Energy reported revenues of $8.6 billion and net income available to common shareholders of $1.02 billion. The company serves over 7 million metered customers and has a market capitalization of approximately $19.8 billion as of June 2024. Its growth profile is driven by significant capital investment in regulated infrastructure, customer and load growth, and a strategic focus on grid modernization and clean energy transition.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: CenterPoint Energy emphasizes reliable, safe, and resilient energy delivery, with a strong focus on customer service, system modernization, and environmental stewardship. Its regulated utility model provides stable returns and cost recovery, while its leadership in grid resiliency, advanced metering, and clean energy transition (including net zero commitments) differentiates it as a forward-looking utility positioned for long-term sustainable growth.
